extracted.intended_audience: DEA registrants, regulated healthcare practitioners, and administrative/regulatory attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register decision ordering revocation of a DEA practitioner registration where the registrant is without state authority to prescribe/dispense controlled substances; explains statutory and procedural bases for default, official notice, and revocation. Useful for understanding legal standards and procedural requirements in DEA administrative adjudications under the Controlled Substances Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default admission and waiver of hearing (21 CFR 1301.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant fails to file a written request for hearing, the registrant is deemed to have waived the right to a hearing and be in default; a default 'shall be deemed to constitute a waiver of the registrant's/applicant's right to a hearing and an admission of the factual allegations of the [OSC].' (21 CFR 1301.43(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When default occurs, unless excused, DEA may file a request for final agency action and the Administrator may enter a default final order pursuant to 21 CFR 1316.67. The Agency treated failure to request a hearing as admission of the OSC allegations and proceeded to final action. (See RFAA citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of service as basis for default
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of the Order to Show Cause must be adequate to support a finding of default (e.g., personal service and acknowledgment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequacy of service can be established by Government declaration(s) (here, a DEA Diversion Investigator's declaration) and a signed Form-DEA 12 acknowledging receipt. The Agency may rely on such evidence in finding that the registrant was properly served and is in default.

rubrics_metrics.name: State licensure/authority prerequisite for DEA registration (21 U.S.C. 823(g)(1) and 21 U.S.C. 802(21))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must be 'authorized to dispense . . . controlled substances under the laws of the State in which he practices' to obtain and maintain a DEA registration; Congress defined 'practitioner' to include those 'licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted' by the State to distribute, dispense, or administer controlled substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency relies on statutory text and Supreme Court precedent (Gonzales v. Oregon) and DEA precedent to hold that possession of state authority to dispense controlled substances is a fundamental condition of DEA registration. Lack of state authority means the registrant is not eligible to maintain a DEA registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation based on state suspension/revocation (21 U.S.C. 824(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General is authorized to suspend or revoke a registration 'upon a finding that the registrant . . . has had his State license or registration suspended . . . [or] revoked . . . by competent State authority and is no longer authorized by State law to engage in the . . . dispensing of controlled substances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the undisputed evidence shows the registrant lacks authority to practice in the State of registration (e.g., 'No License due to Discipline' status), the Agency will revoke the DEA registration. The decision here ordered revocation for that reason and denied pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'dispense' and 'practitioner' under applicable state law (N.C. Gen. Stat. 90-87)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under North Carolina law, 'dispense' includes delivering a controlled substance by or pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner, including prescribing, administering, packaging, labeling, or compounding; 'practitioner' means a physician or other person licensed, registered or otherwise permitted to distribute, dispense, conduct research with respect to or to administer a controlled substance so long as such activity is within the normal course of professional practice or research in the State (N.C. Gen. Stat. 90-87(8), 90-87(22)(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEA examines state statutory definitions to determine whether the individual is a 'practitioner' authorized to handle controlled substances. If state law requires licensure and the registrant lacks that license, DEA considers the registrant ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice of facts and right to challenge (agency notice and 5 U.S.C. 556(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency 'may take official notice of facts at any stage in a proceeding—even in the final decision.' However, 5 U.S.C. 556(e) provides that when an agency decision rests on official notice of a material fact not appearing in the record, a party is entitled, on timely request, to an opportunity to show the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DEA relies on official notice (e.g., state licensing records), the registrant may file a properly supported motion for reconsideration of findings of fact within fifteen calendar days. The motion and response must be filed and served by email to the other party and to the DEA Office of the Administrator (contact provided in the Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration of registration does not deprive DEA of jurisdiction to conclude proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant allowing the DEA registration to expire during the pendency of an enforcement proceeding does not affect the Agency's jurisdiction or prerogative under the CSA to adjudicate the OSC to finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if registration expired (e.g., registrant's registration expired on July 31, 2025), DEA may continue and conclude the administrative enforcement proceeding and issue a final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies: revocation and denial of pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA may order revocation of the Certificate of Registration and deny any pending applications to renew, modify, or obtain additional registrations if the registrant lacks state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order here revoked Certificate No. MB7242352, denied any pending applications to renew or modify that registration, and denied any other pending applications for additional registration in the State. The agency may set an effective date for the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to sign and publish administrative orders (28 CFR 0.100(b) and administrative practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders are issued pursuant to departmental/regulatory delegation authority (here 28 CFR 0.100(b)) and statutory authority (e.g., 21 U.S.C. 824(a)). An authorized official (Administrator) signs the document; for administrative publication, a DEA Federal Register Liaison Officer may sign electronically without altering legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative processes for submitting the document for Federal Register publication do not alter the legal effect of the signed Order. The Order specifies the effective date and identifies the signing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent and consistent application of statutory principle
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA has consistently applied the principle that revocation of a practitioner's registration is appropriate whenever the practitioner is no longer authorized to dispense controlled substances under state law; the decision cites multiple prior DEA/Federal Register decisions and appellate rulings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites prior DEA decisions (e.g., James L. Hooper, Sheran Arden Yeates, Dominick A. Ricci, Bobby Watts, Frederick Marsh Blanton) and Gonzales v. Oregon to demonstrate consistent application; practitioners/attorneys should consider these precedents when litigating or responding to OSCs.
